thread:
incident-bot: PAGER -> #eng-oncall: SEV2 - sudden NotReady spike in infer-pool-usw-2 (7 nodes). Alerts: node-heartbeat-loss, pod evictions increasing. Grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/inferruntime

alice_k: oncall ack, jumping in :eyes:

tim_sre: I see kubelet restarts on infer-usw-2-{12,13,14}. Kernel logs show watchdog resets. excerpt:
```
[  123.456789] watchdog: BUG: soft lockup - CPU#3 stuck for 22s!
[  123.457001] Killed process 2345 (kubelet) total-vm:...killed by SIGABRT
```

chen_ml: serving runtime pods on those nodes show `CUDA out of memory` followed by crash. sample pod log:
```
E tensorflow/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_driver.cc:xxx] cuCtxPushCurrent failed: CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN
E runtime: oom while allocating kv cache
F runtime: aborting process
```

alice_k: are pods getting evicted or just restarting? any steady leak pattern?

tim_sre: several pods hit CrashLoopBackOff and then kubelet restarted. kubectl snippet:
```
$ kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep infer
inference-abc-1   CrashLoopBackOff   4/5   20m   10.0.0.12   infer-usw-2-12
inference-def-1   Running            1/1   2m    10.0.0.13   infer-usw-2-13
```

leah_platform: suggestion: cordon the 3 flapping nodes, drain them, and scale nodegroup +2 to push traffic to healthy capacity. I'll also flip routing policy to prefer eu-west fallback for sensitive customers.

alice_k: doing cordon & drain now. cmds:
```
kubectl cordon infer-usw-2-12
kubectl drain infer-usw-2-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
output: node cordoned, pods evicted -> pods scheduled onto infer-usw-2-17/18 (new nodes).

infra-bot: cluster-autoscaler: scaling up nodegroup infer-usw-2-ng by 2 nodes (requested at 2026-03-17T21:15:23Z).

deploy-bot: no deploys in last 30m; commit/rollouts clear.

tim_sre: remediation plan: 1) drain and reprovision affected nodes 2) restart kubelet service, 3) disable experimental gpu memory-boost flag in runtime config for next 2h, 4) monitor KV cache allocations and OOMs. I'll remote into node and restart kubelet: `sudo systemctl restart kubelet`

chen_ml: after routing to new nodes and disabling gpu-boost, canary perf checks look good: embedding latencies back to baseline (p50 28ms -> 30ms). no OOMs in last 3 min on restored nodes.

jess_cs: CS update: two customers (CS-4256, CS-4257) reported degraded latency during the spike; informed them we're mitigating, offered temporary routing to eu-west.

alice_k: handing off to night oncall @tim_sre in 20m — I'll stay until nodes stable or until you confirm. current severity set to SEV2 due to customer latency.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: as of +5m, node heartbeats restored for 6/7 nodes. 1 pod still CrashLoopBackOff on infer-usw-2-14 (OOM on startup). Monitoring window 30m.

alice_k: leaving runbook notes in #incidents, will open postmortem ticket with logs + timeline. initial hypothesis: gpu driver/firmware interaction causing transient OOMs + kubelet watchdog leading to restart cascade.

tim_sre: I'll continue with node reprovision and kubelet restart on the last node, and escalate to hardware team if watchdog recurs.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVE: degraded latency resolved, routing normal. follow-up: postmortem required.

alice_k: closing page — will draft postmortem and include mitigation steps (restrict gpu-boost toggle, improve kubelet watchdog backoff, add kv-cache OOM alerts). Thanks all :thumbsup:
